problems.q: How much heat, in joules, warms 40.0 g of water by 5.00 °C? Use c = 4.184 J/g°C (OpenStax AF2e) and round to three significant figures.
problems.why: q = m c ΔT = (40.0 g)(4.184 J/g°C)(5.00 °C) = 836.8 J. Three significant figures rounds that to 837 J. OpenStax AF2e §9.1.
hints: Multiply the mass, 4.184, and the temperature change. Then keep three figures.

problems.q: A reaction has ΔH = −120 kJ. Is the reaction exothermic or endothermic?
problems.why: A negative ΔH means the system gives off heat. The reaction is exothermic. OpenStax AF2e §9.3.
hints: Watch the sign. Heat leaving the system is a negative enthalpy change.
